_comment: This is the JSON payload shape emitted by strategy.pine's alert() calls. Point a TradingView webhook alert at your relay/bot endpoint; the relay is responsible for translating this into a real broker order plus its own risk controls (duplicate-alert guard, daily loss limit, kill switch).

example_buy_alert.optLots: <approx option lots to buy, delta-based — only present when showOptGuidance is on>
example_buy_alert.optNote: approx, delta-based, verify live premium before sizing

example_sell_alert.optLots: <approx option lots to buy (PE side), delta-based — only present when showOptGuidance is on>
example_sell_alert.optNote: approx, delta-based, verify live premium before sizing

_optLots_caveat: optLots is NOT a real premium calculation — it's riskCapital / (underlying_stop_distance * optDelta * optLotSize), an approximation using a fixed assumed delta (default 0.5, ATM-ish). Real option delta moves with moneyness, time to expiry and IV, and the script has no live option chain data. Treat optLots as a rough starting point and re-check against the actual live premium/delta of the strike you intend to trade before sizing a real order. See options-trading-notes.md.
relay_responsibilities: Verify the webhook request actually came from TradingView (e.g. shared secret in the URL or a header check) before acting on it.
Reject/deduplicate repeated alerts for the same bar/signal.

Convert 'action' + 'price'/'stop'/'target' into an actual bracket order via your broker's API (for options: pick the strike/expiry per options-trading-notes.md, and size using your own live premium — optLots is a starting estimate, not a live calculation).
Enforce your own max daily loss / max open positions independent of the strategy.
Log every received alert and resulting order for reconciliation against the TradingView backtest/paper results.
